chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah al-Wasiti, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Abu Khalid, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no group of forty men who gather and supplicate to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, regarding a matter, except that Allah answers them. If they are not forty, then four people supplicate to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, ten times, except that Allah answers them. If they are not four, then one person supplicates to Allah forty times, and Allah, the Almighty, the Compeller, answers him.'

key_terms.رَهْطٍ: A group or company of people

ai.seo_question: How many people need to pray together for their supplication to be accepted?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia emphasis on the efficacy of collective supplication (dua al-jama'ah), establishing specific numerical thresholds—forty men, four men praying ten times, or one man praying forty times—as conditions for guaranteed divine response. Scholars often interpret these numbers as symbolic of completeness and sincerity, reflecting the principle that persistent, unified devotion removes obstacles to acceptance. It underscores the belief in Allah's readiness to answer, reinforcing the spiritual discipline of regular and communal prayer in Shia practice.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Ma’bad, from Ubeydullah Bin Abdullah Al Wasity, from Dorost Bin Abu Mansour, from Abu Khalid who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is none from a group of forty men gathering, supplicating to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic regarding a (particular) matter, except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Answer for them. So if there do not happen to be forty men, so (a group of) four supplicating to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic ten times, except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Answer for them. So if there do not happen to be four, so one individual supplicating to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> forty times, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Mighty, the Compeller would Answer for him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ali ibn Ma’Bad from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Wasiti from Drust ibn abu Mansur from abu Khalid who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘If a group of forty people come together to pray and plead before Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, for help in a matter, Allah will accept their prayers. If they are not forty then four people can pray to Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ten times still Allah will accept their prayer. If four people are not present, then one person can pray forty times. Allah the Most Majestic, the Almighty, will accept his prayer.’”
